summary: Takao Maruyama is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University until 1962. He held teaching posts at Rissho University (attested 1972, 1981), Shinshu University (attested 1983–1984; emeritus attested 2001), and Mejiro University (attested 1988).

Takao Moriyasu (1948–2024) was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and historical studies. Educated at the University of Tokyo and Osaka University, he taught at Kanazawa University, Osaka University (professor 1994–2012), Kindai University, and Kobe City University of Foreign Studies.

Takao Yamagata (1932–2019) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University. He served at Miyagi Gakuin Women's University and was president of the Association for the Study of Indian Religions (attested 1997).

Takashi Iwata is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Waseda University and the University of Hamburg under Albrecht Wezler, Lambert Schmithausen, Akira Hirakawa, and Ernst Steinkellner, he served as a professor at Waseda University (~1993–2015).
Takashi Koezuka is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served at Osaka University as a professor (attested 2001) and later as professor emeritus (attested 2012).
Takashi Maeda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University. He served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1995 and 2006).

Takashi Matsuura is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who completed his B.A. and Ph.D. at the University of Tokyo. He has taught as an assistant professor at the University of Tokyo and as a lecturer at Seitoku, Rikkyo, and Keio.

Takashi Nakao (1931–2020) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history who studied at Rissho University and Tokyo University of Education. He held posts at Bunkyo University Women's College and served as an emeritus professor at Rissho University (1979–2002).

Takashi Ogawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Komazawa University, Peking University, and the University of Tokyo. He taught at Komazawa University from 1991 and became a specially appointed professor at Tokyo International University in 2024.
Takashi Yamada is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied at Hosei University. He served as an associate professor at the Prefectural University of Kumamoto (attested 2003).
Takatoshi Ito is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Komazawa University, where his post is attested in 1981 and 1991.
Takatoshi Nakamura is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ryukai Mano in 1979. He served as a researcher at the Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute at Taisho University (attested 1978).

Takatsugu Hayashi is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Delhi. He has held posts at Sendai National College of Technology, Hosen Gakuen College, and Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Takayasu Higuchi (1919–2015) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Central Asian studies who studied at Kyoto University. He was a professor of archaeology at Kyoto University (~1953–1983) and directed several museums and research institutes.

Takayasu Kimura is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at Taisho University. Attested in 1995, he served as a researcher at the Institute of Modern Religious Education of Shingon Buzan and a lecturer at Taisho University.
Takayasu Suzuki is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1984 to 1994. He served as a professor at Yamaguchi Prefectural University from ~2007 to 2017.

Takayoshi Kamei (1886–1977) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1908–1912). He later held posts at the University of Tokyo, Ibaraki University, and Seisen University.

Takayoshi Namikawa is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his undergraduate and graduate degrees at Bukkyo University. He was appointed professor there in 1981, became professor emeritus in 2018, and was a visiting professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University.

Takayuki Hirosawa is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied under Lambert Schmithausen at the University of Hamburg. He has held positions at Taisho University, including a professorship attested in 2014.

Takehiro Sueki (1921–2007) was a philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1941–1944). He held posts at the University of Electro-Communications (~1955–1968), the University of Tokyo (~1968–1982), and Toyo University (~1982–1992).
